newsitem.title: USA: Black named as St.Petersburg police chief.
newsitem.headline: Black named as St.Petersburg police chief.

text.p: The city of St. Petersburg, which was hit by race riots last October, Wednesday appointed its first black police chief.
Assistant Chief Goliath Davis was named by Mayor David Fischer to replace Chief Darryl Stephens, who was promoted to city manager. Stephens replaced Rick Dodge, who resigned.
"The African American community expects the same as the majority community -- fair, professional law enforcement," Davis said at a news conference.
The riots broke out last October after a white police officer shot and killed a black teenager following a traffic stop in a black neighbourhood. The officer said the youth tried to run him down.
Black leaders said the unrest, in which several buildings were burned down and about a dozen people wounded, highlighted racist attitudes in the local police force.
